blockers.quote: The rival has never once thought about you. Your best friend has the next desk, the same chocolate bar, the same exam.
blockers.why: Check #7 Misconception first fails here: the explanation contradicts the established rival who trash-talks you every morning, so the fact does not cleanly break the wrong belief.
blockers.fix: The rival is twenty places ahead and throws that line at everyone. Your best friend has the next desk, the same chocolate bar, the same exam.

blockers.quote: She doesn't ask. You don't say it. And you don't pull back. The brushes stay in the jar.
blockers.why: Check #11 Never say the feeling fails because the narration repeats the mouth, doorway and brushes already shown in the preceding shot.
blockers.fix: For once, silence leaves both of you in the room.

suggestions.quote: Text her, and never see her colour again. Or take the bus to the warehouse and say it to her face.
suggestions.fix: Owner suggestion: keep the protected dilemma line, then add: “A text would spare her from watching you flinch again.” This gives the loophole a defensible side.

suggestions.quote: You take your bag. And you don't go home. Not that night. Not for a month.
suggestions.fix: Replace with: “You take your bag. And you don't go home that night.” This removes the unexplained three-week housing gap while preserving the month of silence.

suggestions.quote: She's not watching you fail. She's watching the life she handed you walk up the dock with the news. And she wants it in.
suggestions.fix: Replace the final sentence with: “And she's asking you to let her share it.”

keep.quote: Not because of the cards. Because he hears everything first. He always has.
He isn't sawing your chair. He's climbing.
A text would open nothing. You could keep her forever on a screen.
